Unauthenticated by route and authenticated by the provider scheme named in the path — RevenueCat compares a fixed Authorization header. The application is read from the required `applicationId` query parameter, because a provider dashboard is configured per application and the body carries only the provider own shape. Every delivery is stored under the provider event id, so a retry is recognised and applied once.

post.description: Returns the entitlement decision for the signed-in user in one application. Both `applicationId` and `entitlement` are required in the body — the server never guesses which right is being asked about. The answer carries two clocks: `periodEndsAt` is when the paid period stops, and `trustedUntil` is how long a device may act on this answer offline, which is the sooner of `periodEndsAt` and the offline trust window. `hasHistory` says whether this account ever held any subscription row, which is what decides if a paywall needs a Restore button.
